text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to tell U.S. President Bill Clinton: We must keep qualitative edge in the Middle East.
- Elyakim Rubinstein becomes Israel's attorney-general.
- Report: Prime minister ignores Palestinian Authority ploys in Jerusalem.
- Fourth-quarter investments down 23 percent. GDP growth slows to 3 percent from 6 percent over previous six years.
- Koor, Sheraton set up regional hotel chain.
- ECI Telecom and Belgium's leading telecommunications operator Belgacom in $30 million deal.
- Central bank: Union Bank, Bank Leumi charge highest commissions.
- No spinoff of Bank Hapoalim holdings before sale.
- Elscint and GE form 50/50 joint venture.
- U2, rock-and-roll champions of human rights and political correctness and one of the world's biggest attractions, to make first visit to Israel on September 29.
GLOBES
- Netanyahu decides: No further structural changes in Bank Hapoalim to be implemented before its sale.
- Scitex expected to show loss of $30 million in fourth-quarter '96 results today.
- Dollar at record 3.342 shekels.
HAARETZ

- American official: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad is delaying renewal of talks because of his declining health. Netanyahu, starting his visit to Washington, takes a dim view of U.S. F-16 sales to Saudi Arabia.
- Wide gap in Israeli and Palestinian positions on eve of negotiations over Gaza Strip airport. Israel demands full security control as at Rafah and Allenby crossings.
- Poll: 45 percent of Tel Aviv children suffer from breathing diseases because of air pollution.
- Rise of unemployment in Israel's developing towns; in nine places it's more than 10 percent.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu will support budget cut and oppose further tax increases.
- Transport Ministry programme: El Al will be sold to workers and public and able to fly on Jewish sabbath.
- Netanyahu to Clinton: Syria must decide if it wants peace.
- Tomorrow: the interim report on the helicopter disaster in which 73 Israeli soldiers were killed.
- Bank branches to strike tomorrow for five-day week.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk: Without a withdrawal from all of the Golan Heights there will be no peace.
- Government secretly decided on regulations against labour strikes.

- U.S.-held Abu Marzook, ahead of planned extradition to Israel, tells Yedioth Ahronoth: I'll not stop my Hamas activities and would be ready to shake Netanyahu's hand if a solution is found to the Palestinian problem.
- January inflation forecast -- a day before the announcement -- 0.5 to 0.7 percent.
